title: SSH: keys, agents, port forwarding and tunnels

videos.script: Most of the machines an IT person looks after are somewhere else. A server in a cupboard, a web server in a data centre, a PC in another city. The tool for reaching them is SSH, the secure shell. {{remote}} SSH gives you a terminal on the other machine, over an encrypted connection. It proves the server to you, with a key the server holds. And it proves you to the server, with a password or, better, with a key of your own. {{keys}} In this lesson you will make that first connection and check the server's fingerprint. You will make a key, install it, and let an agent remember its passphrase for you. {{steps}} Then you will reach the office from home, through the router. You will hop through the office to a server that only trusts the office. And you will carry a web page through SSH that is not on the network at all. {{reach}} Last, you will close the door to passwords, read who has been knocking, and meet the warning SSH shows when a server's key changes. {{close}}
